## Executive Insight


This book highlights the latest advances in brewing science, technology, and sustainability. It brings together insights from next-generation ingredients and genetically modified yeasts to resource-efficient production methods. Additionally, the book addresses key industry challenges and opportunities. And, it also explores fast-growing market segments such as low- and no-alcohol beer, spiked cider, and other emerging beverage innovations


## Why This Research Matters


The brewing industry is navigating changing consumer preferences, sustainability pressures, and increasing demand for product innovation. This publication provides brewers, researchers, and industry professionals with the latest scientific knowledge and practical solutions to address these challenges. By covering topics ranging from advanced brewing techniques to low- and no-alcohol beer production, the book helps bridge the gap between scientific research and commercial brewing applications.


## About the Authors


This publication brings together contributions from leading brewing scientists, industry experts, and academic researchers from around the world. Edited by Charles Bamforth, the book compiles peer-reviewed scientific research, industry case studies, and practical brewing expertise across multiple areas of brewing science and technology.


IFF Master Brewer[Jens Magnus Eiken](https://www.iff.com/experts/jens-magnus-eiken/) also contributes to the publication, sharing insights drawn from his extensive experience and dedicated career in the beer and brewing industry.


## Practical Applications in Food Biosciences


The contribution made by Jens Magnus Eiken offers a comprehensive exploration of lager beer production. The chapter provides practical guidance for brewers. And it also celebrates the artistry of crafting authentic and innovative lagers tailored to consumer preferences around the globe. The chapter:


- Delves into the latest, research-based knowledge on delivering beer quality
- Covers topical developments and trending areas in beer brewing, such as haze control, gluten-free beer, and low-alcohol beer
- Considers issues of sustainability and the future of beer
- Provides practical, applicable knowledge for hands-on use


## How This Research Was Conducted


The book compiles peer-reviewed research, technical expertise, and practical industry knowledge to provide a comprehensive overview of current advances in brewing science and technology.


Each chapter was authored by subject matter experts with extensive experience in their respective fields. Among the contributors, Jens Magnus Eiken, IFF Master Brewer & Business Product Director Brewing, H&B, IFF, authored the chapter on lager production techniques, drawing on both scientific principles and practical brewing experience. This chapter also examines the key stages of lager production, including raw materials, fermentation, maturation, process control, and quality considerations, while highlighting innovations that help brewers meet evolving consumer expectations and production challenges.


By combining scientific rigor with real-world brewing expertise, the book provides actionable insights for brewers, researchers, and beverage manufacturers seeking to improve quality, efficiency, sustainability, and product innovation across the brewing value chain.
